sanskrit: saṃdaśyamāno 'pi tathā kṛmiṇā tena bhārata guruprabodhaśaṅkī ca tam upaikṣata sūtajaḥ
english: Though he was being gnawed in this way by that worm, O Bhārata, the son of the charioteer, fearing to wake his teacher, simply endured it.

sanskrit: karṇas tu vedanāṃ dhairyād asahyāṃ vinigṛhya tām akampann avyathaṃś caiva dhārayām āsa bhārgavam
english: But Karṇa, by his steadfastness, suppressed that unbearable pain, and without flinching, without showing distress, held the descendant of Bhṛgu upon his lap.

sanskrit: yadā tu rudhireṇāṅge parispṛṣṭo bhṛgūdvahaḥ tadābudhyata tejasvī saṃtaptaś cedam abravīt
english: But when the bearer of the Bhṛgu line felt his body touched by the blood, the radiant one awoke, and, distressed, he spoke these words:

sanskrit: aho 'smy aśucitāṃ prāptaḥ kim idaṃ kriyate tvayā kathayasva bhayaṃ tyaktvā yāthātathyam idaṃ mama
english: "Alas, I have been rendered impure! What is this that is being done to you? Set fear aside and tell me the truth of this matter."

sanskrit: tasya karṇas tadācaṣṭa kṛmiṇā paribhakṣaṇam dadarśa rāmas taṃ cāpi kṛmiṃ sūkarasaṃnibham
english: Then Karṇa told him of the worm's devouring, and Rāma beheld that worm, which resembled a boar,

sanskrit: aṣṭapādaṃ tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraṃ sūcībhir iva saṃvṛtam romabhiḥ saṃniruddhāṅgam alarkaṃ nāma nāmataḥ
english: eight-footed, with sharp fangs, bristling as if covered with needles, its body all hedged with hairs, Alarka by name.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭamātro rāmeṇa kṛmiḥ prāṇān avāsṛjat tasminn evāsṛksaṃklinne tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: No sooner was that worm seen by Rāma than it gave up its life there, drenched in blood; and this seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe dadṛśe viśvarūpaḥ karālavān rākṣaso lohitagrīvaḥ kṛṣṇāṅgo meghavāhanaḥ
english: Then in the sky there appeared a rākṣasa of every form and terrible aspect, red of throat, dark of limb, borne upon a cloud.

sanskrit: sa rāmaṃ prāñjalir bhūtvā babhāṣe pūrṇamānasaḥ svasti te bhṛguśārdūla gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam
english: With palms joined, his heart fulfilled, he addressed Rāma: "Blessings upon you, O tiger of the Bhṛgus! I shall now depart whence I came.

sanskrit: mokṣito narakād asmi bhavatā munisattama bhadraṃ ca te 'stu nandiś ca priyaṃ me bhavatā kṛtam
english: I have been delivered from hell by you, O best of sages. May good fortune be yours, and joy; you have done me a great kindness."

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahābāhur jāmadagnyaḥ pratāpavān kas tvaṃ kasmāc ca narakaṃ pratipanno bravīhi tat
english: The mighty-armed and majestic son of Jamadagni said to him: "Who are you, and why did you fall into hell? Tell me that."

sanskrit: so 'bravīd aham āsaṃ prāg gṛtso nāma mahāsuraḥ purā devayuge tāta bhṛgos tulyavayā iva
english: He replied: "In an earlier time I was a great asura named Gṛtsa, in the age of the gods, dear one—a contemporary, as it were, of Bhṛgu himself.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ bhṛgoḥ sudayitāṃ bhāryām apaharaṃ balāt maharṣer abhiśāpena kṛmibhūto 'pataṃ bhuvi
english: I carried off by force the beloved wife of Bhṛgu, and by the curse of the great sage I became a worm and fell to the earth.

sanskrit: abravīt tu sa māṃ krodhāt tava pūrvapitāmahaḥ mūtraśleṣmāśanaḥ pāpa nirayaṃ pratipatsyase
english: Your forefather said to me in his wrath: 'Feeding on urine and phlegm, O wicked one, you shall pass into hell.'

sanskrit: śāpasyānto bhaved brahmann ity evaṃ tam athābruvam bhavitā bhārgave rāma iti mām abravīd bhṛguḥ
english: 'Let there be an end to the curse, O brahman,' I said to him then; and Bhṛgu answered me: 'It shall come when Rāma appears in the line of Bhṛgu.'

sanskrit: so 'ham etāṃ gatiṃ prāpto yathā nakuśalaṃ tathā tvayā sādho samāgamya vimuktaḥ pāpayonitaḥ
english: So I came to this state, ill-fated as it was; but by meeting with you, O virtuous one, I am freed from that sinful birth."

sanskrit: evam uktvā namaskṛtya yayau rāmaṃ mahāsuraḥ rāmaḥ karṇaṃ tu sakrodham idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having spoken thus and bowed to Rāma, the great asura departed; but Rāma in anger spoke these words to Karṇa:

sanskrit: atiduḥkham idaṃ mūḍha na jātu brāhmaṇaḥ sahet kṣatriyasyaiva te dhairyaṃ kāmayā satyam ucyatām
english: "This pain was extreme, O fool; no brahman could ever endure it. Yours is the steadfastness of a kṣatriya. Speak the truth, by your desire."

sanskrit: tam uvāca tataḥ karṇaḥ śāpabhītaḥ prasādayan brahmakṣatrāntare sūtaṃ jātaṃ māṃ viddhi bhārgava
english: Then Karṇa, afraid of a curse, said to him, seeking to appease him: "Know me, O descendant of Bhṛgu, to be born a sūta, between brahman and kṣatriya.

sanskrit: rādheyaḥ karṇa iti māṃ pravadanti janā bhuvi prasādaṃ kuru me brahmann astralubdhasya bhārgava
english: People on earth call me Karṇa, the son of Rādhā. Be gracious to me, O brahman, O descendant of Bhṛgu, who longed only for weapons.

sanskrit: pitā gurur na saṃdeho vedavidyāpradaḥ prabhuḥ ato bhārgava ity uktaṃ mayā gotraṃ tavāntike
english: A teacher who imparts the knowledge of the Veda is, beyond doubt, a father and a lord; therefore in your presence I claimed the Bhārgava lineage."

sanskrit: tam uvāca bhṛguśreṣṭhaḥ saroṣaḥ prahasann iva bhūmau nipatitaṃ dīnaṃ vepamānaṃ kṛtāñjalim
english: The best of the Bhṛgus, angry yet half-smiling, said to him as he lay fallen on the ground, wretched and trembling, with palms joined:

sanskrit: yasmān mithyopacarito astralobhād iha tvayā tasmād etad dhi te mūḍha brahmāstraṃ pratibhāsyati
english: "Because out of greed for weapons you have deceived me here, therefore, O fool, this Brahmā-weapon shall not appear to you in your memory—

sanskrit: anyatra vadhakālāt te sadṛśena sameyuṣaḥ abrāhmaṇe na hi brahma dhruvaṃ tiṣṭhet kadā cana
english: except at the hour of your death, when you face one who is your equal. For in one who is no brahman, the brahman power can never abide secure.

sanskrit: gacchedānīṃ na te sthānam anṛtasyeha vidyate na tvayā sadṛśo yuddhe bhavitā kśatriyo bhuvi
english: Go now! Here there is no place for falsehood. Yet no kṣatriya on earth shall ever be your equal in battle."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa nyāyenopajagāma saḥ duryodhanam upāgamya kṛtāstro 'smīti cābravīt
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, he duly departed; and coming to Duryodhana, he declared, "I am now accomplished in arms."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca karṇas tu samavāpyaitad astraṃ bhārgavanandanāt duryodhanena sahito mumude bharatarṣabha
english: Nārada said: Having gained this weapon from the son of Bhṛgu, Karṇa, together with Duryodhana, rejoiced, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid rājānaḥ samājagmuḥ svayaṃvare kaliṅgaviṣaye rājan rājñaś citrāṅgadasya ca
english: Then once, O king, the kings gathered together at the bride-choosing of Citrāṅgada, the king in the Kaliṅga country.

sanskrit: śrīmadrājapuraṃ nāma nagaraṃ tatra bhārata rājānaḥ śataśas tatra kanyārthaṃ samupāgaman
english: There, O Bhārata, was a splendid city named Rājapura; thither the kings came by the hundreds, seeking the maiden's hand.

sanskrit: śrutvā duryodhanas tatra sametān sarvapārthivān rathena kāñcanāṅgena karṇena sahito yayau
english: Hearing that all the princes were assembled there, Duryodhana went, accompanied by Karṇa, in a chariot adorned with gold.

sanskrit: tataḥ svayaṃvare tasmin saṃpravṛtte mahotsave samāpetur nṛpatayaḥ kanyārthe nṛpasattama
english: Then, O best of kings, when that bride-choosing, a great festival, was under way, the rulers came together for the maiden's sake:

sanskrit: śiśupālo jarāsaṃdho bhīṣmako vakra eva ca kapotaromā nīlaś ca rukmī ca dṛḍhavikramaḥ
english: Śiśupāla, Jarāsaṃdha, Bhīṣmaka and Vakra, Kapotaroman and Nīla, and Rukmī of firm valor,

sanskrit: sṛgālaś ca mahārāja strīrājyādhipatiś ca yaḥ aśokaḥ śatadhanvā ca bhojo vīraś ca nāmataḥ
english: and Sṛgāla, O great king, and he who was lord of the women's realm, Aśoka and Śatadhanvan, and the hero called Bhoja by name,

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āśritāḥ mlecchācāryāś ca rājānaḥ prācyodīcyāś ca bhārata
english: these and many others who dwell in the southern quarter, and kings who were teachers of the mlecchas, and those of the east and north, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kāñcanāṅgadinaḥ sarve baddhajāmbūnadasrajaḥ sarve bhāsvaradehāś ca vyāghrā iva madotkaṭāḥ
english: All wore golden armlets, all bore wreaths of fine gold, all with shining bodies, fierce in their pride like tigers.

sanskrit: tataḥ samupaviṣṭeṣu teṣu rājasu bhārata viveśa raṅgaṃ sā kanyā dhātrīvarṣadharānvitā
english: Then, O Bhārata, when those kings had taken their seats, the maiden entered the arena, attended by her nurse and her chamberlain.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃśrāvyamāṇeṣu rājñāṃ nāmasu bhārata atyakrāmad dhārtarāṣṭraṃ sā kanyā varavarṇinī
english: Then, O Bhārata, as the names of the kings were being proclaimed, that maiden of lovely complexion passed by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu kauravyo nāmarṣayata laṅghanam pratyaṣedhac ca tāṃ kanyām asatkṛtya narādhipān
english: But Duryodhana of the Kuru line did not brook being passed over; he stopped the maiden, slighting the assembled rulers.

sanskrit: sa vīryamadamattatvād bhīṣmadroṇāv upāśritaḥ ratham āropya tāṃ kanyām ājuhāva narādhipān
english: Drunk with the pride of his strength, relying on Bhīṣma and Droṇa, he mounted the maiden upon his chariot and challenged the kings.

sanskrit: tam anvayād rathī khaḍgī bhaddhagodhāṅgulitravān karṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: Behind him followed, O bull among men, the charioteer Karṇa, best of those who bear arms, sword in hand and fitted with leather guard and finger-thongs.

sanskrit: tato vimardaḥ sumahān rājñām āsīd yudhiṣṭhira saṃnahyatāṃ tanutrāṇi rathān yojayatām api
english: Then there arose a mighty tumult among the kings, O Yudhiṣṭhira, as they donned their armor and yoked their chariots.

sanskrit: te 'bhyadhāvanta saṃkruddhāḥ karṇaduryodhanāv ubhau śaravarṣāṇi muñcanto meghāḥ parvatayor iva
english: Enraged, they rushed upon both Karṇa and Duryodhana, loosing showers of arrows like clouds upon two mountains.

sanskrit: karṇas teṣām āpatatām ekaikena kṣureṇa ha dhanūṃṣi saśarāvāpāny apātayata bhūtale
english: As they charged, Karṇa with a single razor-arrow each struck down their bows, with their quivers, upon the ground.

sanskrit: tato vidhanuṣaḥ kāṃś cit kāṃś cid udyatakārmukān kāṃś cid udvahato bāṇān rathaśaktigadās tathā
english: Then some he left without bows, some with bows still upraised, and some still drawing their arrows, their lances and clubs and chariot-spears,

sanskrit: lāghavād ākulīkṛtya karṇaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ hatasūtāṃś ca bhūyiṣṭhān avajigye narādhipān
english: all thrown into disorder by his swiftness. Karṇa, foremost of warriors, vanquished most of those rulers, their charioteers slain.

sanskrit: te svayaṃ tvarayanto 'śvān yāhi yāhīti vādinaḥ vyapeyus te raṇaṃ hitvā rājāno bhagnamānasāḥ
english: Urging on their own horses, crying "Drive! Drive!", those kings, their spirits broken, abandoned the field and fled away.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu karṇena pālyamāno 'bhyayāt tadā hṛṣṭaḥ kanyām upādāya nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: Then Duryodhana, guarded by Karṇa, went on his way, and joyfully bore the maiden to the city named for the elephant.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca āviṣkṛtabalaṃ karṇaṃ jñātvā rājā tu māgadhaḥ āhvayad dvairathenājau jarāsaṃdho mahīpatiḥ
english: Nārada said: Learning that Karṇa had revealed his might, the king of Magadha, the lord of earth Jarāsaṃdha, challenged him to single combat between chariots in battle.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ divyāstraviduṣor dvayoḥ yudhi nānāpraharaṇair anyonyam abhivarṣatoḥ
english: A battle arose between the two, both versed in celestial weapons, as in combat they rained upon each other with weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: kṣīṇabāṇau vidhanuṣau bhagnakhaḍgau mahīṃ gatau bāhubhiḥ samasajjetām ubhāv api balānvitau
english: Their arrows spent, their bows undone, their swords broken, they came down to the earth, and both, endowed with strength, grappled with their arms.

sanskrit: bāhukaṇṭakayuddhena tasya karṇo 'tha yudhyataḥ bibheda saṃdhiṃ dehasya jarayā śleṣitasya ha
english: Then, fighting with the thorn-like strokes of the arms, Karṇa rent apart the joint of his body which Jarā had once knit together.

sanskrit: sa vikāraṃ śarīrasya dṛṣṭvā nṛpatir ātmanaḥ prīto 'smīty abravīt karṇaṃ vairam utsṛjya bhārata
english: Seeing the alteration of his own body, the king said to Karṇa, "I am pleased," and laid aside his enmity, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: prītyā dadau sa karṇāya mālinīṃ nagarīm atha aṅgeṣu naraśārdūla sa rājāsīt sapatnajit
english: Out of affection he then gave to Karṇa the city of Mālinī; and so, O tiger among men, that vanquisher of foes became king among the Aṅgas.

sanskrit: pālayām āsa campāṃ tu karṇaḥ parabalārdanaḥ duryodhanasyānumate tavāpi viditaṃ tathā
english: And Karṇa, crusher of enemy hosts, ruled over Campā with Duryodhana's consent, as is known to you as well.

sanskrit: evaṃ śastrapratāpena prathitaḥ so 'bhavat kṣitau tvaddhitārthaṃ surendreṇa bhikṣito varmakuṇḍale
english: Thus by the splendor of his arms he became renowned upon the earth; and for your benefit the lord of the gods begged of him his armor and his earrings.

sanskrit: sa divye sahaje prādāt kuṇḍale paramārcite sahajaṃ kavacaṃ caiva mohito devamāyayā
english: Bewildered by the god's illusion, he gave away his celestial, inborn earrings, most cherished, and his inborn coat of mail as well.

sanskrit: vimuktaḥ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ ca sahajena ca varmaṇā nihato vijayenājau vāsudevasya paśyataḥ
english: Stripped of his two earrings and of his inborn armor, he was slain in battle by Vijaya, before the very eyes of Vāsudeva—

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasyābhiśāpena rāmasya ca mahātmanaḥ kuntyāś ca varadānena māyayā ca śatakratoḥ
english: by the curse of a brahman and of the great-souled Rāma, by the boon Kuntī had granted, and by the wiles of him of a hundred sacrifices,

sanskrit: bhīṣmāvamānāt saṃkhyāyāṃ rathānām ardhakīrtanāt śalyāt tejovadhāc cāpi vāsudevanayena ca
english: by Bhīṣma's slighting of him, who reckoned him but half a chariot-warrior in the count, by Śalya's draining of his spirit, and by the counsel of Vāsudeva,

sanskrit: rudrasya devarājasya yamasya varuṇasya ca kuberadroṇayoś caiva kṛpasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: and by the weapons of Rudra, of the king of the gods, of Yama and of Varuṇa, of Kubera and Droṇa, and of the great-souled Kṛpa—

sanskrit: astrāṇi divyāny ādāya yudhi gāṇḍīvadhanvanā hato vaikartanaḥ karṇo divākarasamadyutiḥ
english: taking up these celestial weapons, the wielder of Gāṇḍīva slew in battle Karṇa, son of Vikartana, radiant as the day-making sun.

sanskrit: evaṃ śaptas tava bhrātā bahubhiś cāpi vañcitaḥ na śocyaḥ sa naravyāghro yuddhe hi nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: Thus cursed was your brother, and deceived by many; yet that tiger among men is not to be mourned, for he met his death in battle.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etāvad uktvā devarṣir virarāma sa nāradaḥ yudhiṣṭhiras tu rājarṣir dadhyau śokapariplutaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus far, the divine sage Nārada fell silent; but the royal sage Yudhiṣṭhira, drowned in grief, sank into brooding.

sanskrit: taṃ dīnamanasaṃ vīram adhovadanam āturam niḥśvasantaṃ yathā nāgaṃ paryaśrunayanaṃ tathā
english: To that hero, downcast in spirit, his face bowed low, anguished, sighing like a serpent, his eyes brimming with tears—

sanskrit: kuntī śokaparītāṅgī duḥkhopahatacetanā abravīn madhurābhāṣā kāle vacanam arthavat
english: to him Kuntī, her body wrung with grief, her mind stricken with sorrow, sweet of speech, spoke in season these words full of meaning:

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira mahābāho nainaṃ śocitum arhasi jahi śokaṃ mahāprājña śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira, mighty-armed one, you should not grieve for him. Cast off your sorrow, O most wise, and hear these words of mine.

sanskrit: yatitaḥ sa mayā pūrvaṃ bhrātryaṃ jñāpayituṃ tava bhāskareṇa ca devena pitrā dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: Long ago I strove to make known to him his brotherhood with you, O best of the upholders of dharma, and so did the god Bhāskara, his father.

sanskrit: yad vācyaṃ hitakāmena suhṛdā bhūtim icchatā tathā divākareṇoktaḥ svapnānte mama cāgrataḥ
english: All that a friend desiring his welfare and wishing him prosperity might say—so was he told by the day-maker at the close of a dream, and in my presence as well.

sanskrit: na cainam aśakad bhānur ahaṃ vā snehakāraṇaiḥ purā pratyanunetuṃ vā netuṃ vāpy ekatāṃ tvayā
english: Yet neither could the Sun, nor I, by any motives of affection, win him over of old, nor bring him to union with you.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālaparītaḥ sa vairasyoddhukṣaṇe rataḥ pratīpakārī yuṣmākam iti copekṣito mayā
english: Then, overtaken by fate, bent on kindling the fire of enmity, set on working against you—so I let him be.

sanskrit: ity ukto dharmarājas tu mātrā bāṣpākulekṣaṇaḥ uvāca vākyaṃ dharmātmā śokavyākulacetanaḥ
english: Thus addressed by his mother, the Dharma-king, his eyes clouded with tears, the righteous one, his mind distraught with grief, spoke these words:

sanskrit: bhavatyā gūḍhamantratvāt pīḍito 'smīty uvāca tām śaśāpa ca mahātejāḥ sarvalokeṣu ca striyaḥ na guhyaṃ dhārayiṣyantīty atiduḥkhasamanvitaḥ
english: "Because of your keeping the secret hidden, I am stricken," he said to her; and that one of great splendor, overcome with deep sorrow, laid a curse: that throughout all the worlds women should hold no secret concealed.

sanskrit: sa rājā putrapautrāṇāṃ saṃbandhisuhṛdāṃ tathā smarann udvignahṛdayo babhūvāsvasthacetanaḥ
english: That king, remembering his sons and grandsons, his kinsmen and his friends, became troubled at heart and sick in mind.

sanskrit: tataḥ śokaparītātmā sadhūma iva pāvakaḥ nirvedam akarod dhīmān rājā saṃtāpapīḍitaḥ
english: Then, his soul wrapped in grief like a fire wrapped in smoke, the wise king, tormented by anguish, gave himself over to despair.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yudhiṣṭhiras tu dharmātmā śokavyākulacetanaḥ śuśoca duḥkhasaṃtaptaḥ smṛtvā karṇaṃ mahāratham
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But Yudhiṣṭhira, righteous of soul, his mind distraught with grief, mourned, burning with sorrow, as he remembered Karṇa, the great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: āviṣṭo duḥkhaśokābhyāṃ niḥśvasaṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ dṛṣṭvārjunam uvācedaṃ vacanaṃ śokakarśitaḥ
english: Possessed by pain and grief, sighing again and again, looking upon Arjuna, worn down by sorrow he spoke these words:

sanskrit: yad bhaikṣam ācariṣyāma vṛṣṇyandhakapure vayam jñātīn niṣpuruṣān kṛtvā nemāṃ prāpsyāma durgatim
english: "Had we lived by begging in the city of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, rather than leaving our kinsmen bereft of their men, we would not have come to this misery.

sanskrit: amitrā naḥ samṛddhārthā vṛttārthāḥ kuravaḥ kila ātmānam ātmanā hatvā kiṃ dharmaphalam āpnumaḥ
english: Our enemies, the Kurus, had their wealth and their ends fulfilled, it seems; but having slain ourselves by our own hands, what fruit of dharma do we gain?

sanskrit: dhig astu kṣātram ācāraṃ dhig astu balam aurasam dhig astv amarṣaṃ yenemām āpadaṃ gamitā vayam
english: A curse upon the kṣatriya way of life! A curse upon strength of breast! A curse upon the wrath by which we have been brought to this calamity!

sanskrit: sādhu kṣamā damaḥ śaucam avairodhyam amatsaraḥ ahiṃsā satyavacanaṃ nityāni vanacāriṇām
english: Good are forbearance, self-restraint, purity, freedom from enmity, freedom from envy, non-injury, and truthful speech—these are the constant virtues of those who dwell in the forest."
